title: Jumping spider, level jump over 45 mm — Phidippus regius
citation: Nabawy M.R.A., Sivalingam G., Garwood R.J., Crowther W.J., Sellers W.I. (2018). Energy and time optimal trajectories in exploratory jumps of the spider Phidippus regius. Scientific Reports 8: 7142. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-25227-9 — video: Supplementary Movie S2, 'Level jumps' montage, middle panel.
licence: CC BY 4.0 — video and data reused with attribution; panel cropped and overlays added by Pixels to Proof.
note:
**The published video cannot verify this number, and the tool says why.** (1) Gravity check: at the stated 3,200 fps and the 45 mm platform gap, the flight curves at 12.4 m/s² instead of 9.81. (2) Free-flight check: the spider slows down sideways at 69% of its vertical acceleration; free flight gives about 0. (3) The montage skips frames: one long step every 13–14 frames, found in all three level-jump panels (12 in this one); the tool put them back in the timeline before fitting. The 30 mm and 60 mm jumps fail the same way (gravity +42% and +39%, sideways 46% and 31%).

The video alone cannot tell which cause it is: the silk safety line the spider attaches before jumping (the authors found no strong evidence that it mattered), motion towards the camera, or other editing of the time base. This is a verdict about the published video, not about the authors' measurement, which was made on the original 3,200 fps recordings.
provenance: Supplementary Dataset S3, sheet 'Regius', row S/N 8: gap x = 45 mm, y = 0 mm; take-off velocity 0.838 m/s, take-off angle 18 deg, time to take-off 21.875 ms. No uncertainty is published. Methods: the nominal centre of mass was tracked in Phantom PCC 2.7 and the ballistic velocity and angle were chosen to minimise the RMS deviation from the trajectory.
